extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to remote code execution. The user-controlled `name` query parameter (declared at app/main.py:19) is interpolated into the `content` string at app/main.py:38 via an f-string, then that string is compiled and rendered as a Jinja2 template at `Template(content).render()`. Because the user input becomes part of the template source before parsing, an attacker can submit `?name={{7*7}}` (evaluated to 49) or Jinja2 gadget chains such as `{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}` to achieve arbitrary code execution. Jinja2's `Template()` constructor does not autoescape or sandbox evaluation.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message:
Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The user-supplied `name` query parameter and the untrusted `public_ip` value (sourced from an external HTTP service response at app/main.py:36) are inserted directly into an HTML string via an f-string without any HTML escaping: `f"

Hello, {name}!

Public IP: {public_ip}

"`. The result is returned as an `HTMLResponse`. An attacker can submit `?name=` to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Jinja2 `Template(...).render()` is used without autoescaping, so no encoding is applied.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Hardcoded secret token in production configuration. `SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN = "5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n"` embeds a credential directly in source code instead of loading it from an environment variable (the adjacent FIXME comment confirms it should be `os.getenv("SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN")`). Anyone with source access obtains the token, and it cannot be rotated without a code change. The token is committed to version control.

Hardcoded secret value in configuration. `SUPER_SECRET_NAME = "John Ripper"` hardcodes a value labeled as secret directly in source code rather than loading it from the environment (the FIXME comment indicates it should use `os.getenv("SUPER_SECRET_NAME")`). Sensitive values should not be committed to version control.
